Chapter 16 of 19

The Endless Stair

Wreck Beach
The story

At the far western edge of the city, a long wooden staircase drops through the trees toward Wreck Beach. Everyone agrees there is a beautiful beach at the bottom. Nobody agrees on how many steps it takes to get there, and the people who make it down describe the beach differently every time.

The stair is the city's way out. It feeds something Terminal City cannot make for itself: scale, sky, sea, the feeling of leaving the useful world behind for a while. People stand at the bottom and feel small and glad about it, and the city receives that too. The stairs know when you are counting. Stop, and they add steps.

The Outer Circuit cannot quite contain it. The Beyond starts somewhere past the bottom. Sometimes the fog comes up the stairs instead of in from the sea. Step down. Beautiful beach. Somewhere below. Never the last.

Field notes
The ruleIf you stop counting, the staircase adds steps.
Where
From the city
Connections
  • Terminal Fog — may rise from below
  • The Outer Circuit — cannot fully contain it
  • The Beyond — can be conceptually reached through the larger “leave and return” function even if the physical staircase is not a literal portal

Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented. Photograph reality. Alter the evidence. Never illustrate the whole myth.
